en: Another noteworthy feature GitHub Copilot
offers to you
is its Code Actions feature.
For example, if I select this code here, I
get these sparkles here
and that's the Code Actions icon that should
pop up when you select code.
If you click it, you get some smart
suggestions which may differ depending on
what you selected
that are suggested by the GitHub Copilot
extensions.
For example, here
I get the suggestion to rewrite this
selected code by modifying it with using
Copilot.
If I click that, it simply opens the inline
chat with that code selected and I can ask
questions as you learned it before.
Or alternatively, I could review it. And if
I click that, it behind the scenes uses
GitHub Copilot Chat to ask for suggestions
regarding how this selected code could be
optimized.
And it displays
the comments it has here in this overlay
window.
In my case here, it does not suggest any
changes, but that might differ depending on
which code you selected.
So it's a nice way of getting a second
opinion on your code to find out whether
there's something you might wanna change or
improve.
And that's this Code Actions feature here.
If you, for example, have an error,
if I remove a key here, you also get such
code actions if you click this light bulb.
Here you get some other suggestions as well,
which come directly from Visual Studio Code,
but you also get the suggestion to fix this
with Copilot.
So if you can't figure out why you have an
error here, you can click this
and it automatically asks GitHub Copilot for
the fix. So here, for example, it tells me
that I need to fix the import statement and
it then suggests the fix down there and I
can now accept it to automatically apply it.
So that's the Code Actions feature, which is
also a feature you should be aware of.
